reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 16 question-paper pages and PDF pages 21–40 of the combined Ordinary Level scheme (the Paper 2 title page 21, the scale table on page 22, the summary of mark allocations on page 23, every Paper 2 model solution and marking note on pages 24–39, and the back cover on page 40). Each task boundary is the published scale beside its model solution, cross-checked against the printed summary.
sourceNotes: The paper is 300 marks: candidates answer all nine questions (Section A Q1–6, 25 marks each; Section B Q7 60 marks, Q8 50 marks, Q9 40 marks). Every question is retained.

39 independently marked units, matching the printed summary of allocations on scheme page 23. Q3(a)(i)+(ii), Q3(b)(i)+(ii), Q5(b)(i)+(ii), Q6(a)(i)+(ii) and Q7(a)(i)+(ii)+(iii) each share one printed scale and are one task.

Paper 2 bands from the 2018 Ordinary scale table on scheme page 22, which differ from Paper 1’s: 5A 0,5; 5B 0,2,5; 5C 0,2,3,5; 5D 0,2,3,4,5; 10B 0,5,10; 10C 0,3,7,10; 10D 0,2,5,8,10; 15D 0,4,7,11,15. Every part prints the same ladder beside its scale.

This paper had no authored cards before this review; all 39 units are new. Marking points are lifted line by line from the scheme (read through the glyph repair map) and labelled with the part of the scheme they come from; the scheme’s bullets are not reproduced, and its Misreading notes keep their own label. The Q3(b) probability table is quoted as one multi-line point. The ticked Q7(f)(ii) box is named in the row label.

Nine parts carry the SEC’s own print of their scheme row (model solution and every credit band), cropped from the scheme PDF and shown only after the reveal: Q1(a)(i), Q6(a), Q7(f)(i) and Q7(f)(ii), whose model solutions are a completed table, a construction, a scatterplot and a tick box printed as images, and Q8(e), Q8(f), Q9(a)(i), Q9(a)(iii) and Q9(b)(i), where a stacked fraction’s denominator or numerator is filtered as a mark cell.

The question booklet is LC003GLP200EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003GLP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 1. Scheme page references are PDF positions (printed page number + 3); question-paper PDF positions match the printed page numbers.

A car distributor sells Ford cars and Renault cars. It has 30 cars for sale on a particular day; 18 are Ford cars and 12 are Renault cars. 7 of the Ford cars are red and 4 of the Renault cars are red. One of the 30 cars is chosen at random. What is the probability that the car chosen is a Ford car or a car which is not red?

cards.stem: A game, called Rainbow, uses an unbiased circular spinner. The spinner has seven sectors coloured red (R), orange (O), yellow (Y), green (G), blue (B), indigo (I), and violet (V) as shown below. The table below shows the angle of each sector. It also shows the cash prize that a player wins if the spinner stops in that sector. Colour, Angle, Probability, Prize: Red, 72°, _, €20; Orange, 30°, _, €60; Yellow, 45°, 1/8, €24; Green, 90°, _, €8; Blue, 60°, _, €42; Indigo, 18°, _, €90; Violet, 45°, _, €48.
cards.questionText: (i) Complete the “Probability” column of the table which shows the probability of the spinner coming to rest in each sector after one spin. (ii) Find the expected value of the prize that a player wins if they play Rainbow.
